name: Experience
features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

5. UNLOCKABLE AUTOMATION (department heads earned through achievements; the player wants to struggle first and feel accomplishment): Ops Control duty manager (unlock: 25 sectors with no illegal duty) handles routine delays and sick call-ins with the player's default rules; Maintenance planner (unlock: first C-check completed on time) auto-books A-checks into maintenance nights; Crew scheduling desk (unlock: 2 months at >= 98% crew coverage) repairs the roster after disruptions and manages extra crew; Commercial analyst (unlock: 5 contracts completed) scores offers vs the fleet and suggests counter-prices; Credit control (unlock: first late government payment collected) chases late payers and sets terms; Fleet & positioning planner (unlock: first widebody) proposes ferry/positioning plans and tech stops; Custom alert & auto-pause rules (unlock: reputation 'Reliable'). Each is a hire with a monthly salary and a skill level that can make mistakes, can be overridden or switched off, and never takes the big decisions (which contracts, which aircraft, crises). Unlock moments are celebrated.

14. ACHIEVEMENTS, SOUND & TUTORIAL HINTS (sound now fully specified in S below; it overrides the sound wording here): achievements for milestones (with a gallery on the Company screen and calm unlock toasts); calm optional sound and ambient audio generated with WebAudio (no audio files needed unless tiny ones are justified): soft UI clicks, inbox chime, cockpit-style ding for decisions, a DISTINCT urgent sound for CREW SHORTAGE (the player already chose it: see S), faint airport/cabin ambience — all with a Settings master switch and volume, OFF by default if autoplay rules require; gentle first-time tutorial hints per screen (dismissible, 'don't show again', reset in Settings), written for an ACMI insider (no condescension).

S. AVIATION SOUND SET (player, 23 Oct; calm sounds for calm situations, urgent sounds for urgent ones). Synthesize with WebAudio so they sound like real airliner cabin/cockpit chimes: sine/triangle partials with a natural bell decay and slight room reverb. No harsh beeps. These meanings are fixed by the player:
- HIGH chime (single, soft): routine info, e.g. a new inbox message or a crew member joined.
- LOW chime (single, soft, like the seat-belt ding): calm timeline events, e.g. a flight departed or landed (off by default as too frequent; toggle), pause and resume.
- HIGH-LOW chime (the classic two-tone 'bing-bong'): NEW CONTRACT offer arrived; a softer variant when a contract is signed.
- DOUBLE high-low: MEDIUM emergency, a decision needed soon, e.g. AOG, a delay with penalty risk, a sick call, a late payer, an offer about to lapse, a world event touching our flights.
- TRIPLE high-low: SERIOUS emergency, e.g. a flight about to be cancelled, airspace closed on an active flight, cash below zero, an evacuation request, a client relationship collapsing.
- URGENT ALARM (distinct, master-caution style, short and repeated a few times, never endless): used ONLY for CREW SHORTAGE and CREW OUT OF HOURS. Both share this one sound.
- The rest is up to you. Examples:
  - achievement unlocked: a warm ascending three-note chime;
  - department head hired or unlocked: a pleasant flourish;
  - soft UI clicks and toggles;
  - optional faint ambience (airport terminal or cabin hum), OFF by default.
Each event maps to exactly one sound, in a single table in code (src/ui/sound.ts or similar), and is documented in docs.
- Volume and settings:
  - Rate-limit and merge bursts: at 4× speed never machine-gun chimes; play the highest-priority sound once per short window.
  - Settings: master on/off, master volume, and per-category toggles (alerts, chimes, UI clicks, ambience).
  - A 'Test sounds' list where each sound can be played with its meaning.
  - iOS/Safari: unlock audio on the first tap. Respect the silent switch where the browser does.
  - Default ON at a moderate volume after the first tap, except ambience, which stays OFF.

T. CREW OUT OF HOURS (new alert, player request): a separate alert and plain-language card for when a pilot or flight attendant has reached a legal limit (FDP or duty, cumulative 7/28-day or 12-month hours, or rest not met), distinct from CREW SHORTAGE (a seat with nobody to fill it).
- It gets its own inbox and alert type and its own icon.
- The four-line card says who, which limit, by how much, and the fixes (replace, delay for rest, sub-charter...).
- Crew Control handles it like a shortage.
- It uses the URGENT ALARM sound (same as crew shortage).

U. COMMANDER'S DISCRETION IS NEVER PLANNED (player, ex-cabin crew; EASA ORO.FTL.205(f)): discretion is only for UNFORESEEN circumstances at or after reporting, decided by the commander near the end of the duty as an emergency measure. It can never be counted in planning or agreed when signing a contract.
- Audit everything and make sure discretion is excluded from:
  - 'Longest day' (fleet card, market, refit preview, popover);
  - contract feasibility and pricing;
  - the roster planner;
  - trip moves;
  - offer generation (no impossible offers);
  - restPlan.
- In Crew Control, offer 'Commander's discretion' only after the crew has reported and only for an unforeseen delay. It is never offered before report or for a planned schedule, and the reason is shown in plain words.
- The fleet card's 'Longest day: 13 h · up to 17 h' means extra pilots resting on board. Make the popover say so plainly and say that discretion is never planned.

V. GAME-WIDE LANGUAGE PASS (player request: 'a lot of redundancy'). Go through every player-facing string (cards, offer and feasibility lines, inbox, toasts, glossary, What's new, tooltips, Crew Planning verdict lines) and remove repetition and filler. Plain, short, insider-correct aviation English. Never lose information.
- Known examples:
  - 'You can't fly Corendon's Winter sun to Corfu for Corendon as it stands' (client named twice);
  - the Crew Planning verdict line repeating the numbers shown right above it.
- Keep the four-line card format.
- Produce a before/after list of the main changes in the update doc.

W. CREW SLIP AT A FUEL STOP (player said yes): on a long one-way flight with a tech stop, a fresh crew is positioned to the stop by airline ticket and takes over, so the duty day splits in two. Examples: Dili→Lisbon via PNH+OTP; Madrid→Singapore via IST.
- The slip crew rests in a hotel at the stop as needed.
- Offers that are too long for one crew become flyable with a slip, priced in (tickets, hotel, extra crew). The v0.8 'no impossible offers' rule then counts a slip as a valid plan.
- Feasibility shows 'Crew change at IST (fresh crew flies in)'.
- The roster plans it, and the map shows the slip crew's deadhead.
- Plain-language explanation in the glossary.

X. WHAT'S NEW CATCH-UP (player won't play v0.8 before v0.9): on the first launch of v0.9, the pop-up shows v0.9, v0.8 and v0.7.4 (everything newer than v0.7.3), newest first. This is a one-time catch-up even if v0.8's pop-up was already seen. Afterwards it is the normal rule.

Y. SMALL FOLLOW-UPS FROM THE v0.8 RELEASE:
- A departure delay can make an augmented cabin crew rest plan impossible after the aircraft left. The pre-departure check stops at report time; it must re-check at departure and fix or alert (crew out of hours).
- 747-400 economics: make sure a well-chosen big job (Hajj, troop, UN, full charters) is profitable for an old 747 without making it generally easy. Today the bot loses about 20% on general work with it.
- The bot runtime target (12 s) is still missed: profile and speed up if cheap.


BASE (already released, in the tree): v0.8 World (client relationships New→Partner, Hajj/UN/VIP/deportation/evacuation/medical/music tours/Antarctica, real rivals, market cycles, world events, dry lease, mixed crews) with v0.7.4 Crew & Cabin (crew planning by sets + round-up hire, researched refit costs + 48 h quick reconfiguration, client-paid cabins, curtained seat rest on every aircraft, bunks always a pair, 767 never bunks, short Longest-day line, no rest marks on art) and the v0.8 fix pack (seats = passengers, body check, no impossible offers, dominated private jet hidden, 'in refit', Boeing 747-400 available, Newcomer noise, staffing = sets, What's-new shows all unseen versions, freeze safety net in core/safety.ts). Earlier: v0.7.3 In-flight Rest & EASA, v0.7.2.x Trip swap & Check planning, v0.7.2 Crew Rules & Fleet, v0.7.1 Crew Control & plain language. Every new problem gets the four-line plain-language card. Add a v0.9 entry at the top of src/data/whatsNew.ts.
